findings.reason: a coordinator dispatching verbatim from the followup never queues §11, so the four duplicated-fact repairs are never built and §11's done-when never runs.
findings.text: `f-wil-001` is the only open dispatch order, and its title and body enumerate §3, §4, §8, §5, §6, §7 and §10 while omitting §11, which is `implementable`, writes `cli.py` alongside §7 and `telemetry_index.py` alongside §5, and declares `depends-on` §7

findings.reason: §4 was deliberately left `implementable` until its open snapshot repair landed, so the same rule applied to §10 keeps its status honest or adds the repair as a followup rather than as prose in a comment nothing tracks.
findings.text: the §10 close comment records that the post-swap service entered a "restart loop, which the coordinator stopped; its repair is in flight", yet the same commit sets §10 `done`

findings.reason: a reader checking §10's landing is sent to §6's evidence, so §10's record is unreadable at the anchor it names and needs repointing once its own anchor is written.
findings.text: the §10 landed comment links `evidence`, the same href §6's own close comment uses, and `docs/evidence/archive/watch-index-lifecycle-landed.html` has no `#s10` anchor

findings.reason: the second branch makes `segments` a written-but-never-read column, reproducing the defect §11 exists to remove in a column the done-when's two greps do not cover, so a node may take that branch and pass.
findings.text: §11 item 3 offers "the column and its assertion are deleted, or the reader uses the column" as equal ways to leave one source of the counter difference, but `counter_diff` is unread today precisely because `_counter_window_rows` (imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_index.py:2126-2131) rebuilds the difference from `segments`, whose only other production appearances are the two writes at imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_index.py:1787 and :1794

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — the §10 landed comment's evidence href points at `#s6`, and the landed archive carries `id="s3"`, `id="s4"`, `id="s5"`, `id="s6"`, `id="s8"` but no `id="s10"`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §10 is declared `done` in the same document whose §10 close comment records an unresolved restart loop and an in-flight repair, and no followup carries that repair.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every gate named in §11 ("on the fleet allocation") is the same durable-placement convention the landed sections used, and the report's own evidence sits under the run's report directory.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §11's heading and body name mechanisms (`name_id`, `_snapshot_paths`, `counter_diff`) rather than tickets, stages or versions; the four claims it folds come from review records, not from a plan identifier.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §11 item 3's second alternative ("the reader uses the column") does not leave one source of the counter difference: it leaves `segments`, the column that is read today, written but never read.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §11 carries four small dedup items, but they share one goal (one owner per index fact) and share three files, so one verdict closes it.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §11 is implementable and writes `cli.py`, `telemetry_index.py`, `index_placement.py` and three test files, but the only open dispatch followup (`f-wil-001`) orders §3, §4, §8, §5, §6, §7, §10 and never §11.
